To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a codon optimized pAcy1 synthetic gene was expressed in E. coli and that the inclusion bodies formed were solubilized and the enzyme was purified to homogeneity by co-expressing chaperones and by affinity chromatography.
a synthetic gene for porcine N-acyl-L-aminoacyl hydrolase 1 (pAcy-1) was cloned and expressed in E. coli.
the optimized gene was cloned into vector and co-expressed with chaperones in E. coli, and that this resulted in high yields of highly active recombinant pAcy1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel expression system for the production of pAcy1.
the development of an efficient expression system for pAcy 1 in the prokayotic host E. coli.
the development of an efficient expression and purification protocol for pAcy-1, which is a promising biocatalyst for the production of N-protected amino acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pAcy1 is best expressed in the presence of molecular chaperons in the E. coli strain BL21 (DE3).
the described expression and purification system is the most efficient one to obtain pAcy1 in a highly active state.
the combination of codon optimization and molecular chaperone co-expression is the most promising strategy to achieve high yields of soluble and active pAcy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pAcy1 is a suitable model enzyme to study the influence of codon adaptation and molecular chaperone co-expression on recombinant expression in E. coli.
the combination of codon optimized gene and molecular chapersones is the most effective approach for pAcy aminoacylase production in E. coli.
the combination of codon optimization, molecular chaperones, and a suitable affinity tag is an excellent approach to obtain highly active and pure recombinant pAcy1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
codon optimization and co-expression of chaperones are key elements for the efficient production of pAcy1 in E. coli.
the combination of codon adaptation and molecular chaperone co-expression can be successfully applied to improve expression and purification of pAcy1.
the combination of codon optimization, molecular chaperones and StrepTag affinity purification is a highly effective system to express and purify pAcy1 in E. coli.
